Chapter Two: The Long Calm

Calm is not the absence of wind; it is the absence of information.

The crew invented work, and the work invented grievances.

Consider the counterexample of the Bellerophon, becalmed for six weeks.

Its captain kept a ledger of everything that did not happen.

An opening tag whose attributes span a newline.

That ledger is the earliest surviving instance of the practice.

The objection writes itself: a ledger of non-events proves nothing.

The reply is that it proves the observer was still observing.

Chapter Three & Last

Landfall changes the meaning of everything that preceded it.

The thesis, restated: attention under conditions of no news is the whole skill.

Two qualifications follow, and neither is small.

First, the practice does not scale past a single observer.

Second, it fails entirely once news resumes.
